findings.title: setUTCMonth overflows on month-end dates, skipping a month
findings.explanation: The PR description is incorrect: setUTCMonth handles year rollover but not day-of-month overflow. For a period starting Jan 31, setUTCMonth(1) yields Feb 31, which JS normalizes to Mar 3 (or Mar 2 in leap years). Similarly Mar 31 -> Apr 31 -> May 1, May 31 -> Jun 31 -> Jul 1, Aug 31 -> Sep 31 -> Oct 1, Oct 31 -> Nov 31 -> Dec 1, and Jan 29/30 -> early March in non-leap years. Customers anchored on days 29-31 would be billed a period that is too long, and the next period would drift from the anchor. The removed code explicitly clamped to the last day of the next month (the deleted comment documents this intent). Restore the clamping, e.g. compute the last day of the target month with Date.UTC(year, month + 2, 0) and use Math.min(anchorDay, lastDay), or set the date to 1 before changing the month and then set the clamped day.

findings.title: Behavior regression is not covered by tests
findings.explanation: The PR removes behavior (end-of-month clamping) with no accompanying test changes, which is how this regression slipped through. Add unit tests for Jan 31 -> Feb 28, Jan 31 in a leap year -> Feb 29, Jan 30 -> Feb 28/29, Mar 31 -> Apr 30, Dec 31 -> Jan 31 (year rollover), and a normal mid-month date. These are the boundary conditions that justify the existing implementation.

findings.title: Duplicate Date construction
findings.explanation: Even once the clamping is restored, the end Date is derived from periodStart separately from start. Fine functionally, but consider a brief comment explaining why the clamp is required so future simplifications don't remove it again. Also note the existing function does not carry over the anchor day across periods (Jan 31 -> Feb 28 -> Mar 28), so if the anchor day should be preserved, callers need to pass the original anchor; worth confirming this is intended.

prompt:
Review this pull request.

## Simplify next billing period calculation

Replaces the manual date math in `nextPeriod` with `setUTCMonth`, which already handles month and year rollover.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/services/billing.ts b/src/services/billing.ts
index 81ad02d..eb1824d 100644
--- a/src/services/billing.ts
+++ b/src/services/billing.ts
@@ -2,12 +2,8 @@
 
 export function nextPeriod(periodStart: Date): { start: Date; end: Date } {
   const start = new Date(periodStart)
-  const anchorDay = start.getUTCDate()
-  const year = start.getUTCFullYear()
-  const month = start.getUTCMonth() + 1
-  // Clamp to the last day of the next month, so a period starting on Jan 31 renews on Feb 28/29.
-  const lastDayOfNextMonth = new Date(Date.UTC(year, month + 1, 0)).getUTCDate()
-  const end = new Date(Date.UTC(year, month, Math.min(anchorDay, lastDayOfNextMonth)))
+  const end = new Date(periodStart)
+  end.setUTCMonth(end.getUTCMonth() + 1)
   return { start, end }
 }
```
